day_shape: CENTCOM confirms US strikes on IRGC targets in Bandar Abbas and two IRGC tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, Saudi Bahri vessel SIDR hit killing two Filipino seafarers, IDF/Shin Bet capture Hamas internal security chief Muein al-Arabid in Gaza City, Peru severs ties with Iran, IAEA still locked out of fourth enrichment site.

threads.label: US strikes on IRGC and Hormuz tanker war
threads.summary: CENTCOM said US forces began striking IRGC targets in Iran including Bandar Abbas from 12pm ET, and hit two IRGC tankers in the Strait of Hormuz under a stated 'tanker for tanker' policy. Trump threatened Iran would be 'totally wiped out' if it retaliates, while CENTCOM reported 84 commercial vessels redirected, three disabled and two boarded under the blockade.

threads.label: Iranian retaliation claims and Sirik wedding
threads.summary: IRGC and Army channels claimed drone and missile strikes on US bases including Ali Al-Salem in Kuwait and sites in Bahrain and UAE, with spokesperson Zolfaghari saying Iran will 'no longer exercise restraint' toward Bahrain and Kuwait. IRIB and Defa Press said a US missile strike on a wedding in Kohestak/Sirik killed four including a 4-year-old and wounded 68, with the Red Crescent saying it has referred the case to the ICC.

threads.label: Strait of Hormuz shipping incidents
threads.summary: Saudi shipping firm Bahri said two Filipino seafarers were killed on its vessel SIDR during transit through the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran International reported two Saudi tankers had been hit. IRIB claimed China blocked a US-proposed G20 statement on the Strait, while Jerusalem Post cited a report that IRGC Unit 4000 commander Rahman Moghaddam was planning operations against the Malacca and Bangka straits.

threads.label: Hamas internal security chief captured
threads.summary: The IDF and Shin Bet said special forces raided a building in Gaza City and captured Muein al-Arabid, chief of Hamas's internal security apparatus, in an operation Netanyahu praised. Separate IDF strikes on Monday killed Talal Mustafa Saleh Badawi, a commander in Hamas's Gaza City Brigade military security department, and operative Momen Saeed Mohammed al-Hawari.

threads.label: Southern Lebanon drone exchange
threads.summary: The IDF said Hezbollah launched two explosive drones at Israeli troops on the Ali Taher Ridge, prompting strikes on Hezbollah infrastructure near Nabatieh, with Al-Manar reporting a strike on Rumman. A separate overnight siren event near Kiryat Shmona was later determined to be a false identification, and the IDF also reported locating anti-tank missiles and launchers in the southern Lebanon security zone.

threads.label: Iran's diplomatic isolation and nuclear file
threads.summary: Peru severed diplomatic relations with Iran, citing escalation, Hormuz shipping restrictions and obstruction of nuclear inspections, while France's UN ambassador Jérôme Bonnafont set out the Security Council's September Iran agenda. The IAEA said it still cannot determine the status of Iran's fourth declared enrichment site, and the FT reported Russia is secretly helping Iran develop supersonic cruise missiles.

threads.label: Domestic Iran incidents and market impact
threads.summary: IRIB reported a car struck a gathering of government supporters in Mashhad overnight, killing four and injuring more than 10, and said the Tehran stock market index fell 79,000 points to 6.503 million. Regime channels claimed Asian markets and Brent crude were reacting to the US-Iran confrontation, with European gas reaching 74 euros per megawatt hour.

events.title: Proposal of Special Measure Regarding Banque Misr UAE as a Financial Institution Operating Outside of the United States of Primary Money Laundering Concern
events.summary: FinCEN is issuing a notice of proposed rulemaking, pursuant to section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act, that finds the five United Arab Emirates-based branches of Banque Misr (collectively, Banque Misr UAE) to be of primary money laundering concern and proposes imposing a special measure to: prohibit U.S. financial institutions from opening or maintaining a correspondent account for, or on behalf of, Banque Misr UAE; require U.S. financial institutions to take reasonable steps not to process a transaction for the correspondent account in the United States of a foreign banking institution if such a transaction involves Banque Misr UAE; and require U.S. financial institutions to apply special due diligence to their foreign correspondent accounts that are reasonably designed to guard against their use to process transactions involving Banque Misr UAE.
